stories.title: Spain mourns at least 68 dead after a high-speed train hits another from behind
stories.summary: A Renfe high-speed train ran into the back of a stopped Iryo train near Urda in Toledo province, south of Madrid, killing at least 68 people according to NPR and the BBC; France 24 and RTÉ put the toll at 69. Spain’s transport minister blamed an “inexplicable human error”, saying a train was ordered to move by the rail manager [[adif|Adif]] despite a technical failure that had halted services, The Local reports. Audio reviewed by the BBC appears to show one train cleared to move while another ahead had stalled. Spain has begun three days of mourning, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has promised a full investigation, and Renfe drivers are going ahead with a strike called before the crash over safety concerns.
stories.background: The Local counts four deadly train crashes in Spain in 2026, with 116 deaths in all, almost all of them in two major accidents on high-speed lines. This is the second of those, and it comes ahead of a national election.

stories.title: Israel’s vote leaves no clear winner, and talk turns to a possible new election
stories.summary: With more than 90% of votes counted, the BBC says all signs point to an impasse in the 120-seat [[knesset|Knesset]] and that the most likely outcome may be new elections. The Times of Israel reports Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to stay with his far-right partners, while opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot looks for a path to “bring change”. The Guardian says Israeli police dismissed a claim by Netanyahu’s Likud party that the election was “stolen” by Arab parties, and RTÉ reports a far-right minister has called for the arrest of Arab party leaders over unproven foreign-funding accusations. France 24 says the Central Elections Committee has asked the Shin Bet chief to investigate allegations of foreign interference linked to Qatar.
stories.background: This was Israel’s first general election since the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023 and the wars that followed, and it was widely described as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership. Israel has only ever been governed by coalitions.

stories.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reaches Miami after leaving Brazil against a court order
stories.summary: The defeated Brazilian presidential candidate arrived in Florida by private jet with his family after crossing into Argentina and flying on through Ecuador, according to BBC Verify and the Buenos Aires Times. Brazil’s Federal Police had revoked his passports after he missed a deadline to hand them in, and NPR reports Washington says it will issue him a visa. The BBC says he denies fleeing and claims to be the victim of a coup and persecution, recycling unsubstantiated fraud allegations; he first called himself Brazil’s “true president”, then downgraded that to “leader”. President Lula called his escape “shameful”, and Argentina’s opposition is demanding answers from President Javier Milei’s government.
stories.background: Lula was re-elected on 25 October with 51.78% of valid votes to Bolsonaro’s 48.22%. Bolsonaro, a senator, is the target of several investigations in Brazil.

stories.title: Trump downplays a Vance letter to Iran as the US warns allies of possible new strikes
stories.summary: The Times of Israel reports, citing the Wall Street Journal, that Vice President JD Vance wrote to the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council setting out a framework to restart peace talks, and that the paper says Trump ordered it, which he denies. The National says Trump acknowledged the letter but called it an offer of medical supplies. RTÉ reports US officials have told several regional allies to be ready for possible renewed military action against Iran after next week’s midterms. DW says a ship was reported on fire in the [[strait-of-hormuz|Strait of Hormuz]] off Oman and that Iran claims it shot down another US drone. The Guardian adds that Shell’s profits doubled to $10.8bn in the last quarter as the conflict pushed up oil margins.
stories.background: The US and Israel launched a war on Iran in February. Fighting and the disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have continued despite a US–Iran memorandum of understanding reached in June.

stories.title: A Russian drone strike on a Dnipro station kills at least 13 while a Kherson truce holds
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities say at least 13 people died when a Russian drone hit a platform at Dnipro railway station where a train was parked, RTÉ reports. The Kyiv Independent says it was a jet-powered drone and that, according to Ukrainian Railways, people stayed on the platform despite an air-raid alert. Elsewhere, a six-day ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, tied to a humanitarian mission in Russian-occupied Oleshky, is bringing rare quiet to the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, France 24 reports. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the “battlefield situation” will decide when peace talks begin and ruled out European participation in an upcoming meeting in Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: North Korea fires about 10 ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast
stories.summary: South Korea’s military said North Korea fired around 10 ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast on Thursday, according to Reuters reporting carried by Daily Maverick. DW says the launch comes amid rising border tensions with South Korea and uncertainty over potential nuclear talks with the US, and Reuters says tensions are high ahead of Pyongyang’s end-of-month deadline to activate propaganda loudspeakers.

stories.title: Five days before the midterms, rallies, an Alaska ballot row and court fights dominate
stories.summary: Barack Obama and Donald Trump held rallies in Georgia and Ohio and traded barbs over the Iran war, tariffs and the White House ballroom, Al Jazeera reports, ahead of the [[midterms|midterm elections]] on 3 November. Trump demanded that Alaska candidates be removed after a New York Times investigation linked Democratic operatives to a namesake candidate in the state’s Senate race, and the state’s Republican governor ordered a probe, the BBC says. Reuters reports a judge rejected a Justice Department request to temporarily stop California counting mail ballots from alleged noncitizens. NPR counts 70 House districts where both parties are spending more than six figures on advertising in the final days.

stories.title: Hackers publish details of more than 40,000 US Homeland Security staff
stories.summary: The leak site Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it had released data on more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, Reuters reports. The BBC attributes the release of information on more than 41,000 staff to a group calling itself the Department of Peace. NPR says the hacktivists argued that unmasking ICE agents, DHS staff and contractors was fair play given the government’s lack of transparency. DW says the data reportedly includes names, phone numbers and email addresses across several security agencies, and follows recent breaches involving the FBI and the Defense Department.

stories.title: ECB president Christine Lagarde will step down in February 2027
stories.summary: Christine Lagarde will leave the [[ecb|European Central Bank]] on 7 February 2027, about nine months before her eight-year term ends, Euronews reports. DW says European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is under way. RTÉ describes the announcement as ending months of speculation about her future, and Euronews adds that the bank is due to announce its latest interest-rate decision later on Thursday.

stories.title: Healey’s first UK budget draws criticism over energy-bill help and a bank tax
stories.summary: The Treasury denied a plan to cut the welfare bill before the election, saying the chancellor’s comments were misinterpreted after John Healey said “there will be a reduction in the benefits bill”, the Guardian reports. The Resolution Foundation called the budget “scattergun” and said its energy-bill help gives the rich almost as much as the poor, and a Lloyds executive criticised Healey for linking bank tax rises to energy-bill support. MercoPress says the government aims to spend 3% of GDP on defence by 2030. In Bilston, the BBC reports local people asking for help for small businesses rather than punishment.

stories.summary: Chief Executive John Lee apologised for the November 2025 fire at Wang Fuk Court that killed 168 people, injured 79 and displaced thousands, and Housing Secretary Winnie Ho resigned, France 24 reports. The Straits Times says an independent committee blamed a renovation contractor and consultant as well as four government departments, and Lee pledged reforms. ABC News reports the investigation found a cigarette was the likely cause.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab leaves several dead in Andhra Pradesh and floods villages in Odisha
stories.summary: Reports of the toll differ: The Hindu counts five deaths in Andhra Pradesh, Reuters via the Straits Times says at least six people were killed along India’s eastern coast, and the Kathmandu Post reports seven in Andhra Pradesh. The Hindu says winds gusted up to 150 kmph, more than 1,000 trees were uprooted and crops across 80,500 hectares were affected, and Chief Minister Naidu announced ₹5 lakh for each victim’s family. The Kathmandu Post says more than 180,000 people were evacuated in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as the storm weakened, and that its remnants are bringing rain and landslide risk to Nepal.

Delhi Police granted permission with strict conditions but denied the request for a mock impeachment, saying it received no separate request. Delhi traders say the rally could hit 21 markets and have sought a postponement, estimating losses of up to ₹10,000 crore. The Indian Express quotes Rahul Gandhi urging students to join. Separately, the voter-roll revision known as [[sir|SIR]] remains contested: The Hindu reports Karnataka’s election office figures show about 64.5 lakh electors potentially missing, around 38.41 lakh of them aged 18 to 29.

Reuters, via Daily Maverick, says the foreign ministry also plans to support anti-gang security operations, while Haiti’s electoral council has postponed planned elections. The attack, in a suburb west of Paris, killed one man and wounded five others, including a 12-year-old girl. France 24 says hundreds marched through the town at the weekend in honour of the 26-year-old victim, and that residents are still reeling five days on.

stories.title: Snow trout released into Nainital’s lake will need more than reintroduction to survive
stories.summary: On 27 April 2026, scientists from Kumaun University’s zoology department released the first batch of captive-bred snow trout fingerlings into a cage in Naini lake, Mongabay India reports, and argues the fish need more than reintroduction to survive.

sources.title: Snow trout needs more than reintroduction to survive

stories.title: A fire in Goa’s Vasco guts more than 100 shops
stories.summary: The Indian Express reports a fire in Vasco destroyed over 100 shops. In another Goa story, it says 19 undertrials granted bail are still behind bars, which has caught the attention of the state human rights body.

sources.title: Fire in Goa’s Vasco guts over 100 shops
Granted bail but still behind bars: 19 undertrials catch attention of Goa rights body

stories.title: Women inside Tihar jail keep the Karva Chauth fast, and families book visits
stories.summary: Around 250 to 300 women at Jail No. 6 are observing the festival, and 1,200 visit slots have been booked across Tihar’s jails for Thursday as families seek to meet their relatives, The Hindu reports.

sources.title: Behind bars, a Karva Chauth fast and a wait for the moon at Tihar

stories.title: Chennai steps up estuary dredging to carry monsoon floodwater out to sea
stories.summary: The Water Resources Department is speeding up dredging of estuaries in Chennai to improve the discharge of flood water during the monsoon, The Hindu reports. At a council meeting, the Mayor said she had not been told when Chief Minister Vijay would inspect Northeast monsoon preparations.

sources.title: Water Resources Dept. steps up estuary dredging in Chennai to improve flood water discharge during monsoon
Chennai Corporation Council: Mayor says she was not informed of timing of CM Vijay’s Northeast monsoon inspection

stories.title: Nine dead after an ambulance fire in Pakistan’s Tharparkar
stories.summary: The death toll from the ambulance fire in Sindh’s Tharparkar district rose to nine on Thursday, according to Mithi Deputy Commissioner Hameed Jagirani, Dawn reports. He said the incident happened on Wednesday night and was linked to an oxygen cylinder.

sources.title: Death toll from Thar ambulance fire rises to nine: district official

stories.title: Phuket city issues a red alert as roads flood in heavy rain
stories.summary: A canal has begun rising rapidly and could overflow into homes if the heavy rain persists, the Straits Times reports.

sources.title: Thailand’s Phuket issues red alert as roads flood amid heavy rain

stories.title: Annapurna Circuit trekkers return after this year’s floods
stories.summary: More than 5,300 foreign tourists trekked the route during Dashain, 769 more than in the same period last year, as improving weather and repairs restored access, according to the Kathmandu Post.

sources.title: Annapurna Circuit sees trekking arrivals rebound after floods

stories.title: A rescued fishing cat is released into a Bangladesh tea estate after months of care
stories.summary: The cat was found badly injured and malnourished in northern Bangladesh and was returned to the wild after months of intensive rehabilitation, Mongabay reports. It was released into a tea estate bordering a large forest.

sources.title: Fishing cat rescue-and-release offers potential model for conservation in Bangladesh

stories.title: Rough seas keep fishers ashore in Indonesia’s Maluku Islands as El Niño builds
stories.summary: Fishers in eastern Indonesia say rough seas are keeping them ashore and shrinking their catches as [[el-nino|El Niño]] builds, according to early local monitoring and interviews reported by Mongabay, including a 64-year-old fisher, Yustinus Pesireron.

sources.title: Fishers in eastern Indonesia struggle as rough seas keep them ashore

stories.title: New South Wales passes the law to create the Great Koala National Park
stories.summary: Conservation and community groups celebrated a “historic win” after legislation to create the park passed on 23 October following more than a decade of campaigning, Mongabay reports, although the funding has been controversial.

sources.title: ‘Historic win’: Australian state approves national koala park despite controversial funding

stories.title: Search for a man swept away by floodwater near Santa Teresa in Central Australia
stories.summary: Police say a 60-year-old man is missing after he was reportedly swept off the roof of a vehicle that had become stuck in floodwater, and they are searching with drones and divers, ABC News reports.

sources.title: Police search launched for man swept away in Central Australia flooding

stories.title: Tropical Storm Vance heads for Sinaloa with more heavy rain for northwest Mexico
stories.summary: Rainfall of 75 to 150 millimetres was expected on Wednesday in central and southern Sinaloa, Nayarit, Durango, the southern tip of Baja California Sur and the Jalisco coast, Mexico News Daily reports.

sources.title: Tropical Storm Vance heads toward Sinaloa, bringing more heavy rainfall to northwest Mexico

stories.title: Mexico City investigates the poisoning of dogs in Condesa’s Parque España
stories.summary: Several dogs fell ill after walks in the park, and blue capsules filled with white powder were later found in sausage meat; at least three of the pets died, Mexico News Daily reports.

sources.title: Mexico City opens investigation into fatal poisoning of dogs in Condesa

stories.title: Jalisco and Mexico’s government agree a $1.3 billion plan to clean up Guadalajara’s water
stories.summary: Governor Pablo Lemus announced a “historic agreement” between the state and federal authorities on $1.3 billion of investment in the Guadalajara area’s water supply, Mexico News Daily reports. The same outlet reports that protesters over foul tap water on 11 October have filed complaints alleging they were tortured by Jalisco state police.

sources.title: Jalisco governor details US $1.3B investment in Guadalajara’s water infrastructure: Wednesday’s mañanera recapped
Protesters file complaints with Attorney General’s Office alleging torture at hands of Jalisco state police officers

stories.title: Scott Gillingham wins a second term as Winnipeg mayor
stories.summary: Gillingham took 39.8 per cent of the ballots cast with all polls reporting just before 10 p.m. on Wednesday, CBC News reports. He said the city’s best days are still to come.

sources.title: 'It feels fantastic,' Scott Gillingham says after winning another term as Winnipeg mayor

stories.title: A lifelong Republican leads the fight against data centres in Ohio
stories.summary: NPR reports many Ohioans are unhappy with the state’s rapid build-out of data centres, and that it is a hot issue in the midterms as candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

sources.title: How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio

stories.title: Yorkshire Water is given the lowest environmental rating
stories.summary: The BBC reports the company, which serves 2.4 million homes, says its performance is “not where it needs to be”.

sources.title: Yorkshire Water given lowest environmental rating

stories.title: Testing at a proposed housing site finds “unacceptable” levels of PFAS
stories.summary: The BBC reports a report says contamination at the former RAF Upper Heyford site, where housing is proposed, is the worst in the UK, with “unacceptable” levels of polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

sources.title: Contamination at proposed housing site worst in UK, report says

stories.title: A sea turtle goes back to the ocean after 22 years in a Kerry aquarium
stories.summary: The turtle, affectionately known as the “queen of the shark tank” at Dingle Aquarium, has been released into the sea, RTÉ reports.

sources.title: Turtle returns to sea after 22 years at Kerry aquarium

stories.title: Athens’ Fyli landfill is a health threat that is running out of room
stories.summary: Balkan Insight’s fellowship reports that the landfill at Fyli is out of sight and out of mind for the Greek capital’s residents, but is a looming threat to public health and is running out of time.

sources.title: The Invisible Mountain: A Toxic Wasteland at the End of Athens

stories.title: Protesters in Pristina demand resignations after another killing of a woman
stories.summary: After a woman was murdered at the weekend, protesters took to the streets to demand accountability, high-level resignations and an end to gender-based violence, Balkan Insight reports.

sources.title: Kosovo Protesters Demand Ministerial, Judicial Resignations After Latest Femicide

stories.title: Scientists off Madeira study how fishing bans are bringing ocean life back
stories.summary: Nearly 200 scientists are studying the marine environment off the Desertas Islands, and say “protection is working”, Euronews reports.

sources.title: 'Protection is working': Madeira scientists study how fishing bans are restoring ocean life

stories.title: UAE closes beaches as it works to contain an oil spill from a supertanker
stories.summary: Authorities across the UAE are stepping up efforts to contain the spill off Umm Al Quwain and to limit the damage to marine life, The National reports.

sources.title: UAE oil spill: Everything we know as beaches close and clean-up drive continues

stories.title: An 11-year-old from Egypt wins the Arab Reading Challenge
stories.summary: Mayar Mohammed, who read more than 60 books during the competition, was named winner at a ceremony in Dubai and won a prize of Dh500,000, The National reports.

sources.title: Egyptian girl, 11, wins Dh500,000 Arab Reading Challenge

lighter.title: A woman’s wardrobe turns up in Pompeii with cosmetics and jewels still inside
lighter.summary: Euronews reports a cupboard in Cornelius Maximus’s house held jewels, coins, tools and cosmetics, offering a glimpse of the daily lives of Pompeii’s women before Vesuvius erupted in AD 79.

sources.title: In Pompeii, a woman's wardrobe resurfaces with beauty items and jewels

lighter.title: A new Texas elementary school is named after its beloved custodian
lighter.summary: Marilyn Hampton regularly bought supplies for children and gave them rides, and was honoured at a public meeting, the Guardian reports. Most US schools are named after presidents, historical figures or civil rights leaders.

sources.title: New elementary school in Texas named after beloved longtime school custodian

lighter.title: Researchers in Japan and the US find a gene key to yellow fever mosquito mating
lighter.summary: The Straits Times reports the discovery could lead to new strategies for controlling the insect’s reproduction.

sources.title: Japan and US university researchers identify gene key to mating of yellow fever mosquitoes

lighter.title: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk is set for his first spacewalk
lighter.summary: CBC News reports the Canadian Space Agency astronaut will work outside the International Space Station, about 400 kilometres above Earth, travelling at roughly 7.66 kilometres per second.

sources.title: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk to conduct his 1st spacewalk

lighter.title: A community rallies to save the bacon of some escaped pigs
lighter.summary: Residents have donated thousands of pounds towards the animals’ upkeep, the BBC reports.

sources.title: Community rallies to save bacon of escaped pigs

lighter.title: A 16-year-old’s pothole-reporting platform has logged nearly 3,000 road complaints
lighter.summary: Inspired by an accident that left his parents injured, the Delhi teenager built an AI-powered platform that reports potholes and other road hazards, identifies the department responsible and tracks repairs. The Hindu says Project Sadak has logged 2,927 complaints across Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru and tracked 190 repairs.

sources.title: Delhi teenager’s Project Sadak logs 2,927 road complaints across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru; tracks 190 repairs

lighter.title: A winner claims a C$40 million lotto prize hours before it expired
lighter.summary: The BBC says it is rare for such a large jackpot to go unclaimed.

sources.title: Winner claims massive Canada lotto prize hours before expiration

lighter.title: A Turkish engineer builds a live 3D pixel map of his adopted hometown, Warsaw
lighter.summary: Notes from Poland reports the map features almost 200,000 buildings, moving trams that match their real-life schedules and live weather conditions.

sources.title: Turkish engineer creates live 3D pixel map of adopted hometown Warsaw

sport.result: Milwaukee Brewers win their first World Series title
sport.note: ABC News calls it an underdog story: the small-ball Brewers play in the smallest market in the majors.

sport.result: Naomi Osaka loses to 18-year-old Mia Pohankova at the Pan Pacific Open
sport.note: Al Jazeera says the 144th-ranked Slovak won 6-3, 7-5; Osaka said she will return stronger.

sport.result: Australia pass 400 and build their lead in the deciding Test in Cape Town
sport.note: ABC News's live blog covers day three against South Africa.

sport.result: Australian Diamonds beat the Silver Ferns 68-58 but lose the Constellation Cup 3-1
sport.note: ABC News says a sold-out Melbourne crowd watched the fourth game.

sport.result: Messi’s Inter Miami draw 2-2 with Cincinnati and slip to third in the East
sport.note: Al Jazeera says Cincinnati equalised with a late goal.

sport.result: Stan Wawrinka’s career ends with a defeat in Basel
sport.note: The BBC says the three-time Grand Slam champion lost on an emotional night.

sport.result: Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback in Dubai on Christmas Eve
sport.note: The National says he has not fought since a double jaw fracture in a knockout defeat to Anthony Joshua.

sport.result: Kimi Antonelli is on the brink of becoming F1’s youngest world champion
sport.note: The National says his win in Austin increased his advantage ahead of the Mexico City race.
